The CS experiments, minus the one that does not fit.

C_sim on CS is NOT runnable on a 24 GB card and P14 cannot be tested here.
Measured: CS alone peaks at 18.9 GB, and SimSample raises the sampled-edge count
by roughly 1.4x on graphs whose nodes sit below the sampling budget (the recorded
figures are 1.38x on Photo and 1.36x on Computers) because deterministic top-k
takes every neighbour where sample-with-replacement-then-dedup takes fewer. CS has
89% of its nodes in that band, so the combination needs ~25 GB and OOMs. This is
the second CS arm lost to memory, after DEMO.

Getting there also required a real fix: the SimSample similarity ordering built a
single [E, D] tensor, which on CS is 163,788 x 6,805 = 4.46 GB - past the
2^32-byte boundary where some torch 2.0 CPU gather kernels overflow a 32-bit
offset and segfault. Every CS SimSample run died at ~1.8 min with 721 GB of host
memory free. utils.py now computes it in chunks; verified numerically identical
by analysis/scripts/check_invariance.py. That fix stands regardless of whether
CS ever runs - it would have hit any wide-feature graph.

L_lean on CS does fit, and comfortably: removing pseudo-labelling removes the
full-pool pass, taking the peak from 18.9 GB to 10.8 GB and running several times
faster. CS is the only dataset where the lean configuration is untested, and it
is the tie-breaker for the two-regime story - its anomalies are feature-visible,
so self-training should matter there as it does on Photo.
